knowledge_cards.fact_statement: 2024 YR4 is classified as an S-type asteroid, indicating a stony composition.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Preliminary spectroscopic analysis from the Gran Telescopio Canarias and Lowell Discovery Telescope suggests that 2024 YR4 is either an S-type asteroid (17% of the asteroid population), an L-type asteroid, or a K-type asteroid

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: 2024 YR4 has a rotation period of approximately 19.5 minutes.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Photometric observations by the Very Large Telescope (VLT) and the La Silla Observatory's 1.54-metre (5.1 ft) telescope indicate 2024 YR4 has a rotation period near 19.5 minutes.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The geometric albedo of 2024 YR4 is estimated to be between 0.08 and 0.18.
knowledge_cards.source_span: The possible size range implies a geometric albedo between 0.08 and 0.18, relatively low for a stony asteroid.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The estimated mass of 2024 YR4 is 2.8×108 kg based on a 60 m diameter.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Rescaling the diameter to the now better measured value of 60 m (200 ft) increases the estimated mass to 2.8×108 kg (6.2×108 lb).

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: 2024 YR4 has an elongated shape.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: 2024 YR4 exhibits a retrograde rotation.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: 2024 YR4 has an orbital inclination of 3.41 degrees with respect to the ecliptic.
knowledge_cards.source_span: Since its close approach in December 2024, the asteroid has an orbital period of about 3.99 years (1,458 d) and an orbital inclination of 3.41 degrees with respect to Earth's orbit (the ecliptic).

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: 2024 YR4 reached perihelion on 22 November 2024.

knowledge_cards.fact_statement: The orbit of 2024 YR4 shrinks over time due to the Yarkovsky effect.
